historical_context: First American tanks to arrive in North Africa (Q3 1941). British crews nicknamed them 'Honey' due to their reliability compared to British cruiser tanks. Fast and reliable, used for reconnaissance and mobile operations.

Stuart M3 (Honey).notes: First American tanks in British service. Reliable and fast.

special_rules: Limited Gun (37mm inadequate vs medium/heavy tanks)

strengths: Good armor for a light tank (51mm)
Perfect for reconnaissance and flank screening
Loved by British crews for reliability
weaknesses: 37mm gun inadequate against German medium tanks
Not suitable for main battle line
Small numbers in 1941 (only 12 in division Q3)
tactical_notes.typical_deployment: Reconnaissance, flank screening, pursuit of retreating enemy. Exploit breakthroughs. Avoid direct combat with German Panzer III/IV. Best used for mobility and speed rather than firepower.

phase_6_data_source.notes: First American tanks arriving in small numbers Q3 1941. Highly valued for reliability.
